title: pkg/router/: Backend.Key()-driven reconcile must rebuild breaker + discovery together
answers: What breaks if I add a new RoutesLoader or Backend implementation in pkg/router?
When does the circuit breaker get recreated in pkg/router?
Can one API group be served by multiple Backends in pkg/router?
body:
`router.go:GrafanaRouter.reconcile` treats `Backend.Key()` as the single fingerprint driving three things that must stay consistent: (1) whether the group's handler is rebuilt vs left alone (compared against the stored `handlerEntry.lastKey`), (2) whether a fresh `gobreaker` instance is minted for that group (new key = target may have moved, so the old breaker's state is stale) vs kept across an unchanged-key reconcile, and (3) the discovery docs rebuilt in `publish()` from the live `served` map. A new `Backend`/`RoutesLoader` implementation must implement `Key()` to change whenever the underlying route truly changes, or stale breakers/handlers linger.

The design also assumes one backend owns ALL versions of a group (not per-version backends) — `/apis/{group}` is built by iterating backends 1:1, not merged. Relaxing that invariant requires updating `discovery.go`/`discovery_handler.go` discovery synthesis at the same time, per pkg/router/AGENTS.md.

Separately, `types.go`'s `Backend`/`RoutesLoader`/`Router` interfaces are consumed directly by every implementation (`forward.go`, `dummy.go`, `plugin.go`, `aggregate_*.go`, `st_fallback.go`) plus `reconcile`/`publish`; narrowing or deleting a method requires updating all of them (some methods, like `Router.HandleFunc`'s `next` param, are intentionally unused today as a future-mounting seam — don't remove them as "dead code").
applies: Applies to any change touching Backend/RoutesLoader implementations, reconcile, or discovery synthesis in pkg/router; does not apply to the hot serving path (HandleFunc) which only reads the published snapshot.

Stale breakers/handlers linger if Key() fails to change.
